A is true: the secondary oocyte is a large cell, while the first polar body is a tiny cell.
R is true: meiosis I in the primary oocyte divides the cytoplasm unequally. The secondary oocyte keeps almost all the nutrient-rich cytoplasm, and the polar body gets very little.
This unequal cytoplasmic division is exactly why the secondary oocyte is so much larger. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which event directly induces the rupture of the Graafian follicle and the release of the ovum in the middle of the menstrual cycle?
options: A sharp fall in progesterone secretion
Rapid secretion of LH reaching its maximum level (LH surge)
A gradual decline in FSH secretion
questions.explanation:
LH and FSH both rise during the follicular phase. LH reaches its peak (the LH surge) in the middle of the cycle, around day 14.
The LH surge causes the Graafian follicle to rupture and release the ovum, which is ovulation.
A fall in progesterone and degeneration of the corpus luteum happen at the end of the cycle, when there is no fertilisation. They trigger menstruation, not ovulation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the human testis are correct?
(i) The male reproductive system is located in the pelvis region.
(ii) An adult testis is oval, about 4–5 cm long and 2–3 cm wide.
(iii) Sertoli cells are located in the interstitial spaces between seminiferous tubules.
(iv) Immunologically competent cells are present in the interstitial spaces along with Leydig cells.
(v) The inner lining of a seminiferous tubule is formed by spermatogonia and Leydig cells.
(vi) Each testis is covered by a dense covering.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the male reproductive system is located in the pelvis region.
(ii) Correct: an adult testis is oval, about 4–5 cm long and 2–3 cm wide.
(iii) Incorrect: Sertoli cells line the inside of the seminiferous tubules, not the interstitial spaces.
(iv) Correct: the interstitial spaces contain Leydig cells along with other immunologically competent cells.
(v) Incorrect: the tubule lining is formed by spermatogonia and Sertoli cells, not Leydig cells.
(vi) Correct: each testis has a dense covering.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about human oogenesis are correct?
(i) Oogonia are formed within the fetal ovary during embryonic development.
(ii) The primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division while inside the secondary follicle.
(iii) The first meiotic division of the primary oocyte gives a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body.
(iv) The zona pellucida is a new membrane formed by the secondary oocyte.
(v) The cell released at ovulation has already completed the second meiotic division.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: oogonia form in the fetal ovary during embryonic development.
(ii) Incorrect: meiosis I is completed in the tertiary follicle, not the secondary follicle.
(iii) Correct: meiosis I gives a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body.
(iv) Correct: the secondary oocyte forms a new membrane, the zona pellucida.
(v) Incorrect: a secondary oocyte is released, and it completes meiosis II only after sperm entry.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In human males, the testes are situated outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum.
Reason (R): Spermatogenesis requires a temperature lower than the normal internal body temperature.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: the testes lie outside the abdominal cavity, in the scrotum.
R is true: spermatogenesis needs a temperature about 2–2.5 °C lower than the internal body temperature.
The scrotal position exists precisely to keep the testes at this lower temperature, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the luteal phase, which structure secretes large amounts of progesterone, and what is the main role of this hormone?
questions.explanation:
After ovulation, the remaining cells of the ruptured Graafian follicle form the corpus luteum.
The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which is essential for maintaining the endometrium for implantation.
Option (1) is wrong because ovulation is induced by the LH surge, not by the Graafian follicle's secretion.
Option (4) is wrong because the placenta forms only in pregnancy and does not cause menstruation.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of human oogenesis in the correct chronological order:
A. The primary oocyte becomes surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells.
B. The Graafian follicle ruptures, releasing the secondary oocyte.
C. Oogonia enter meiosis and are arrested in prophase-I.
D. More granulosa layers and a new theca surround the follicle.
E. An antrum appears, and the primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division.
questions.explanation:
C: oogonia enter meiosis and arrest in prophase-I, becoming primary oocytes.
A: each primary oocyte gets a layer of granulosa cells, forming a primary follicle.
D: more granulosa layers and a new theca form the secondary follicle.
E: the tertiary follicle develops an antrum, and the primary oocyte completes meiosis I.
B: the mature Graafian follicle ruptures and releases the secondary oocyte.
The order is C, A, D, E, B. Meiosis I is completed only after the theca stage.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When the Graafian follicle ruptures at ovulation in a human female, the cell released from the ovary is the:
options: Primary oocyte that is still arrested in prophase I
Ootid formed after the second meiotic division
Secondary oocyte, which has not yet completed meiosis II
Oogonium that is about to begin meiosis
questions.explanation:
The primary oocyte completes meiosis I inside the tertiary follicle and becomes a secondary oocyte.
At ovulation, the Graafian follicle ruptures and releases this secondary oocyte. It has not yet completed meiosis II.
Meiosis II, which produces the ootid and the second polar body, is completed only after a sperm enters.
The tempting option (2), ootid, fails because the ootid forms only after sperm entry.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A researcher examines a section of a testis. Type P cells sit in the lining of the seminiferous tubules alongside dividing germ cells. Type Q cells lie in clusters in the spaces between the tubules, near small blood vessels. A chemical selectively destroys only the type Q cells. Which effect would appear first?
options: Germ cells inside the tubules lose their nutritional support
The testes can no longer be kept below body temperature
Spermatogonia disappear from the tubule lining immediately
questions.explanation:
Type Q cells lie in clusters in the interstitial spaces near blood vessels, so they are Leydig (interstitial) cells. Type P cells line the tubules with germ cells, so they are Sertoli cells.
Leydig cells synthesise and secrete androgens. Destroying them first causes androgen secretion to fall sharply.
Option (1) fails because Sertoli cells nourish germ cells, and they are intact.
Temperature control is done by the scrotum, and spermatogonia are not destroyed immediately.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The signals that initiate parturition originate from the maternal pituitary gland.
Statement II: The inner cell mass contains stem cells that have the potency to give rise to all tissues and organs.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. The signals that start parturition come from the fully developed foetus and the placenta. They first cause mild uterine contractions (the foetal ejection reflex). The maternal pituitary only responds afterwards by releasing oxytocin.
Statement II is correct. NCERT states that the inner cell mass contains stem cells with the potency to give rise to all tissues and organs.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of structures through which sperms pass from their site of formation to the outside?
options: Seminiferous tubule → Vasa efferentia → Rete testis → Epididymis → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Urethra
Seminiferous tubule → Rete testis → Epididymis → Vasa efferentia → Vas deferens → Urethra → Ejaculatory duct
Seminiferous tubule → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Urethra
Seminiferous tubule → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Vas deferens → Epididymis → Ejaculatory duct → Urethra
questions.explanation:
Sperms form in the seminiferous tubules. They pass to the rete testis, then the vasa efferentia, and then the epididymis.
From the epididymis they enter the vas deferens. It joins the seminal vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct, which opens into the urethra.
Correct order: Seminiferous tubule → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Urethra.
Option (1) swaps rete testis and vasa efferentia, and option (4) places the vas deferens before the epididymis.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Besides contributing to the seminal plasma, the secretion of which male accessory glands also helps in lubrication of the penis?
questions.explanation:
The male accessory glands are the seminal vesicles, the prostate and the bulbourethral glands. All three contribute to seminal plasma.
NCERT notes that the bulbourethral glands' secretion also helps lubricate the penis.
Seminal vesicles and prostate add to seminal plasma, but NCERT does not credit them with lubrication.
Leydig cells are not accessory glands. They are interstitial cells of the testis that secrete androgens.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the human testis, the seminiferous tubules open into the vasa efferentia through the:
questions.explanation:
NCERT pathway: seminiferous tubules → rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct.
So the seminiferous tubules open into the vasa efferentia through the rete testis.
The epididymis, vas deferens and ejaculatory duct all come later in the pathway.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about gametogenesis in humans are correct?
(i) Oogonia are formed in the fetal ovary, and no new oogonia are added after birth.
(ii) Primary oocytes remain temporarily arrested in prophase-I of meiosis.
(iii) The primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division while inside the primary follicle.
(iv) Each secondary spermatocyte contains 23 chromosomes.
(v) The secondary oocyte completes its second meiotic division before it is released at ovulation.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: oogonia form in the fetal ovary, and no new oogonia are added after birth.
(ii) Correct: primary oocytes stay temporarily arrested in prophase-I of meiosis.
(iii) Incorrect: the primary oocyte completes meiosis-I inside the tertiary follicle, not the primary follicle.
(iv) Correct: secondary spermatocytes are haploid, with 23 chromosomes each.
(v) Incorrect: the secondary oocyte completes meiosis-II only after a sperm enters it, not before ovulation.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Absence of menstruation in a woman of reproductive age always indicates pregnancy.
Reason (R): During pregnancy, all events of the menstrual cycle stop and there is no menstruation.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true: during pregnancy all events of the menstrual cycle stop, so there is no menstruation.
A is false: NCERT says a missed period only may indicate pregnancy. It can also result from other causes such as stress or poor health. So 'always' makes the assertion wrong.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Surgical removal of both testes in an adult male would also impair the normal functioning of his seminal vesicles and prostate.
Reason (R): The functions of the male sex accessory ducts and glands are maintained by androgens secreted by the Leydig cells of the testes.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true: NCERT states that androgens from the Leydig cells keep the male accessory ducts and glands functioning.
A is true: removing both testes removes the Leydig cells, the main source of androgens. Without androgens, the seminal vesicles and prostate cannot function normally.
R therefore directly explains why A happens.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) GnRH
(b) LH
(c) FSH
(d) Androgens
List-II
(i) Acts on Sertoli cells to stimulate secretion of factors that help spermiogenesis
(ii) Hypothalamic hormone acting on the anterior pituitary
(iii) Stimulate the process of spermatogenesis
(iv) Stimulates Leydig cells to synthesise androgens
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(a) GnRH is a hypothalamic hormone that acts on the anterior pituitary, so (a)-(ii).
(b) LH stimulates Leydig cells to synthesise androgens, so (b)-(iv).
(c) FSH acts on Sertoli cells, which secrete factors that help spermiogenesis, so (c)-(i).
(d) Androgens stimulate the process of spermatogenesis, so (d)-(iii).
The correct matching is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The presence or absence of the hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity or sexual experience.
Reason (R): The hymen can be torn by a sudden fall or jolt, insertion of a tampon, or sports like cycling and horseback riding, and in some women it persists even after coitus.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: the presence or absence of the hymen does not show whether a woman has had sexual experience.
R is true: the hymen can tear from a sudden fall or jolt, a tampon, or sports like cycling and horseback riding. In some women it also persists after coitus.
R explains A: because the hymen can break without coitus and stay intact after coitus, its condition cannot indicate virginity.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The menstrual phase of the human menstrual cycle lasts about ____ days, and the menstrual flow results from ____.
options: 3–5; breakdown of the endometrial lining of the uterus and its blood vessels
3–5; breakdown of the myometrium of the uterus
questions.explanation:
The menstrual flow lasts about 3–5 days.
It results from the breakdown of the endometrial lining of the uterus and its blood vessels, which forms a liquid that leaves through the vagina.
The myometrium is the muscular layer of the uterus and is not shed.
Follicle rupture is ovulation, not menstruation.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the later phase of human pregnancy, the hormone relaxin is secreted by the:
questions.explanation:
NCERT: in the later phase of pregnancy, the ovary secretes relaxin.
The tempting wrong option is the placenta. The placenta secretes hCG, hPL, estrogens and progestogens, but not relaxin.
The anterior pituitary and the endometrium do not secrete relaxin.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During cleavage, the human embryo that consists of 8 to 16 blastomeres is called the:
questions.explanation:
Key NCERT fact: as the zygote undergoes cleavage, the embryo with 8–16 blastomeres is called a morula.
The morula keeps dividing and becomes the blastocyst as it moves into the uterus. So option (1), the blastocyst, is a later stage and is wrong.
The zygote is the single-celled stage.
The trophoblast is only the outer cell layer of the blastocyst, not a whole embryo stage.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A woman has a regular 28-day menstrual cycle, and in this cycle the ovum is NOT fertilised. Starting just after the menstrual phase ends, arrange the following events in the correct order:
(a) LH surge
(b) Large-scale secretion of progesterone by the corpus luteum
(c) Regeneration of the endometrium while follicles grow and secrete estrogens
(d) Degeneration of the corpus luteum
(e) Menstrual flow as the endometrium breaks down
questions.explanation:
(c) Follicular phase: growing follicles secrete estrogens, and the endometrium regenerates.
(a) Mid-cycle LH surge: this triggers ovulation around day 14.
(b) Luteal phase: the corpus luteum forms from the ruptured Graafian follicle and secretes large amounts of progesterone.
(d) No fertilisation: the corpus luteum degenerates.
(e) Progesterone falls, the endometrium breaks down, and menstrual flow follows.
Option (3) fails because progesterone from the corpus luteum cannot come before the LH surge and ovulation.
The correct order is c → a → b → d → e.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following hormones is NOT produced in a woman exclusively during pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: during pregnancy the placenta secretes hCG and hPL, and the ovary secretes relaxin. These hormones are made only in pregnancy.
Prolactin is secreted by the anterior pituitary in non-pregnant women as well. Its level only rises several-fold during pregnancy.
hCG, hPL and relaxin are therefore pregnancy-specific, but prolactin is not.
Trap: relaxin may seem like an ordinary ovarian hormone, but NCERT lists it as produced only during pregnancy.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about human sperm and semen are correct?
(i) The acrosome is a cap-like structure over the anterior part of the haploid nucleus and is filled with enzymes that help in fertilisation.
(ii) The mitochondria that power tail movement are located in the neck of the sperm.
(iii) For normal fertility, at least 60 per cent of the ejaculated sperms must show vigorous motility.
(iv) Secretions of the epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate are essential for maturation and motility of sperms.
(v) Androgens maintain the functions of the male sex accessory ducts and glands.
(vi) The plasma membrane of a sperm covers only its head region.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the acrosome is an enzyme-filled cap over the anterior part of the haploid nucleus.
(ii) Incorrect: the mitochondria lie in the middle piece, not the neck.
(iii) Incorrect: the 60% figure refers to normal shape and size. Only 40% of sperms need vigorous motility.
(iv) Correct: secretions of these ducts and glands are essential for sperm maturation and motility.
(v) Correct: androgens maintain the male accessory ducts and glands.
(vi) Incorrect: the plasma membrane covers the whole body of the sperm.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Normally only one sperm fertilises a human ovum, even though many sperms reach it.
Reason (R): Acrosomal secretions help the sperm pass through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane into the cytoplasm of the ovum.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: normally only one sperm fertilises the ovum (monospermy).
R is true: acrosomal secretions help the sperm pass through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane into the ovum's cytoplasm.
However, R does not explain A. Monospermy is ensured because sperm contact with the zona pellucida changes the membrane and blocks entry of other sperms. Acrosomal enzymes only help a sperm get in.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Fimbriae help in collecting the ovum after ovulation.
Reason (R): Fimbriae are finger-like projections present at the edges of the isthmus.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: fimbriae are finger-like projections that help collect the ovum after ovulation.
R is false: fimbriae are found on the edges of the infundibulum, the part of the oviduct closest to the ovary. They are not on the isthmus, which is the narrow part joining the uterus.
So A is true but R is false.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following cells are haploid?
Spermatogonium, primary spermatocyte, secondary spermatocyte, spermatid, primary oocyte, first polar body, ootid, zygote
questions.explanation:
Cells formed after meiosis I (the reduction division) are haploid.
Haploid cells in the list:
- secondary spermatocyte
- spermatid
- first polar body
- ootid
Diploid cells in the list:
- spermatogonium and primary oocyte (formed by mitosis, or before meiosis begins)
- primary spermatocyte
- zygote (formed by fusion of two haploid gametes)
That makes 4 haploid cells. The usual trap is forgetting that the first polar body is also haploid.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the human female reproductive system are correct?
(i) Each ovary is about 2 to 4 cm long and is attached to the pelvic wall and uterus by ligaments.
(ii) The ovarian stroma is enclosed by a thin epithelium and is differentiated into an outer medulla and an inner cortex.
(iii) The isthmus is the wider part of the oviduct, and it opens into the ampulla.
(iv) Each fallopian tube is about 10-12 cm long and extends from the periphery of the ovary to the uterus.
(v) The uterus is single, shaped like an inverted pear, and supported by ligaments attached to the pelvic wall.
(vi) The ovaries are primary sex organs that produce the ovum as well as several steroid hormones.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: each ovary is 2–4 cm long and is attached to the pelvic wall and uterus by ligaments.
(ii) Incorrect: the cortex is the outer (peripheral) zone and the medulla is the inner zone.
(iii) Incorrect: the isthmus is the narrow last part of the oviduct and joins the uterus. The ampulla is the wider part.
(iv) Correct: each oviduct is 10–12 cm long and runs from the ovary to the uterus.
(v) Correct: the uterus is single, inverted pear-shaped and held by ligaments.
(vi) Correct: the ovaries are primary sex organs that produce the ovum and steroid hormones.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about a human sperm are correct?
(i) The head contains an elongated haploid nucleus.
(ii) The acrosome covers the posterior portion of the nucleus.
(iii) The plasma membrane envelops only the head region.
(iv) The middle piece possesses numerous mitochondria.
(v) The sperm is composed of a head, neck, middle piece and tail.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: The head contains an elongated haploid nucleus.
(ii) Incorrect: The acrosome covers the anterior portion of the nucleus, not the posterior.
(iii) Incorrect: The plasma membrane envelops the whole body of the sperm.
(iv) Correct: The middle piece has numerous mitochondria.
(v) Correct: A sperm has a head, neck, middle piece and tail.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about human oogenesis are correct?
(i) The primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division within the tertiary follicle.
(ii) A primary follicle is surrounded by both granulosa cells and a theca layer.
(iii) The secondary oocyte produced by meiosis I is haploid.
(iv) Degeneration of follicles between birth and puberty reduces their number in the ovary.
(v) The ootid is released from the ovary at ovulation.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the primary oocyte completes meiosis I within the tertiary follicle.
(ii) Incorrect: a primary follicle has only granulosa cells around it. The theca first appears in the secondary follicle.
(iii) Correct: meiosis I halves the chromosome number, so the secondary oocyte is haploid.
(iv) Correct: follicles degenerate between birth and puberty, so their number falls.
(v) Incorrect: a secondary oocyte is released at ovulation. The ootid forms only after sperm entry.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Loss of androgen secretion in an adult male would impair the maturation and motility of sperms even after they have been released from the seminiferous tubules.
Reason (R): The functions of the male sex accessory ducts and glands, whose secretions are essential for sperm maturation and motility, are maintained by androgens.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true: Androgens maintain the functions of the male accessory ducts and glands. These are the epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate.
A is true: Sperms mature and gain motility after leaving the seminiferous tubules, with the help of these accessory secretions. Losing androgens would therefore impair maturation and motility.
R explains A: Androgen loss disrupts exactly the secretions that sperm maturation and motility depend on.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Mitotic divisions of the zygote, called cleavage, begin as it moves through the isthmus of the oviduct towards the uterus.
Statement II: The embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a blastocyst.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I: Correct. Cleavage is the mitotic division of the zygote. It starts as the zygote moves through the isthmus of the oviduct towards the uterus, giving 2, 4, 8 and 16 blastomeres.
Statement II: Incorrect. The embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is the morula. The morula keeps dividing and becomes the blastocyst as it moves further into the uterus.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The secondary oocyte completes its second meiotic division before it is released from the Graafian follicle.
Statement II: The second meiotic division of the oocyte is unequal and produces a second polar body and a haploid ootid.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. The ovum leaves the Graafian follicle at ovulation as a secondary oocyte. Its meiosis II is completed only when a sperm enters it during fertilisation.
Statement II is correct. Meiosis II is unequal: most of the cytoplasm goes to the haploid ootid, and a small second polar body is formed.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Suppose 100 primary spermatocytes in a seminiferous tubule complete both meiotic divisions normally. How many secondary spermatocytes and how many spermatids, respectively, will be formed?
questions.explanation:
Given: 100 primary spermatocytes complete meiosis I and meiosis II.
Meiosis I: each primary spermatocyte forms 2 secondary spermatocytes, so $100 \times 2 = 200$.
Meiosis II: each secondary spermatocyte forms 2 spermatids, so $200 \times 2 = 400$.
Unlike oogenesis, no polar bodies are formed. All four products of each primary spermatocyte are functional.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An experimental toxin selectively destroys only those cells in the testis that lie in the interstitial spaces and synthesise androgens. All other testicular cells remain intact. Which outcome is most likely?
options: Androgen secretion falls and spermatogenesis is impaired, even though spermatogonia and Sertoli cells are still present inside the seminiferous tubules
Sertoli cells stop nourishing the germ cells, but androgen levels stay normal because spermatogonia take over androgen secretion
Androgen secretion is unaffected because Sertoli cells are the main source of testicular androgens
Spermatogenesis continues normally because it depends only on the lower scrotal temperature
questions.explanation:
Interstitial cells that synthesise androgens are Leydig cells.
Androgens stimulate spermatogenesis. If Leydig cells are lost, androgen levels fall and sperm production is impaired, even though spermatogonia and Sertoli cells survive.
Sertoli cells nourish germ cells but do not secrete androgens, so (2) and (3) fail.
A low scrotal temperature is necessary for spermatogenesis but is not sufficient on its own, so (4) fails.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The scrotum helps maintain the temperature of the testes at a level that is
options: about 2–2.5 °C higher than the normal internal body temperature
about 2–2.5 °C lower than the normal internal body temperature
about 5–6 °C lower than the normal internal body temperature
equal to the normal internal body temperature
questions.explanation:
Key NCERT fact: the testes lie outside the abdominal cavity in a pouch called the scrotum.
The scrotum keeps the testicular temperature about 2–2.5 °C lower than the internal body temperature, which spermatogenesis needs.
A higher or equal temperature (options 1 and 4) would impair sperm production.
A 5–6 °C drop (option 3) overstates the NCERT figure.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (part of sperm) with List-II (feature/function):
List-I
(A) Acrosome
(B) Middle piece
(C) Tail
(D) Plasma membrane
List-II
(I) Envelops the whole body of the sperm
(II) Contains enzymes that help fertilisation
(III) Its movement gives the sperm motility
(IV) Contains numerous mitochondria
Choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation:
A – Acrosome: Contains enzymes that help fertilisation (II).
B – Middle piece: Contains numerous mitochondria (IV).
C – Tail: Its movement gives the sperm motility (III).
D – Plasma membrane: Envelops the whole body of the sperm (I).
So the match is A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Scientifically, the sex of a human baby is determined by the father and not by the mother.
Reason (R): All ova carry an X chromosome, whereas half of the sperms carry an X chromosome and half carry a Y chromosome.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true. Females are XX, so every ovum carries an X chromosome. Males are XY, so half of the sperms carry X and half carry Y.
A is true. An X-bearing sperm gives an XX zygote (female). A Y-bearing sperm gives an XY zygote (male).
Since the ovum always contributes X, the sperm alone decides the sex. R therefore correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (time during human pregnancy) with List-II (developmental feature):
List-I
A. After one month
B. By the end of second month
C. During the fifth month
D. By the end of 24 weeks
List-II
I. Limbs and digits develop
II. Eyelids separate and eyelashes are formed
III. Heart is formed
IV. First foetal movements and hair on the head appear
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. After one month of pregnancy, the heart is formed, so A-III.
B. By the end of the second month, limbs and digits develop, so B-I.
C. During the fifth month, the first foetal movements and hair on the head appear, so C-IV.
D. By the end of 24 weeks (second trimester), the eyelids separate and eyelashes form, so D-II.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The gamete mother cells formed in large numbers within each fetal ovary during embryonic development are called:
questions.explanation:
Key fact: during fetal development, a couple of million gamete mother cells, called oogonia, form in each ovary. No more are formed or added after birth.
Primary follicles appear later, when primary oocytes become surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells. So (1) is wrong.
Granulosa cells are follicle cells, not gamete mother cells.
Ootids are not the term NCERT uses for these cells.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following structures are parts of the female external genitalia?
Mons pubis, labia majora, cervix, clitoris, fimbriae, hymen, labia minora, isthmus
questions.explanation:
External genitalia in the list: mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, hymen and clitoris. That makes 5.
Not external:
- Cervix: the lower narrow part of the uterus.
- Fimbriae and isthmus: parts of the oviduct (fallopian tube).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following cells are haploid?
Spermatogonium, primary spermatocyte, secondary spermatocyte, spermatid, spermatozoon
questions.explanation:
Spermatogonium: diploid ($2n = 46$).
Primary spermatocyte: still diploid ($2n$). The number is reduced only when it completes meiosis I.
Secondary spermatocyte: haploid ($n = 23$).
Spermatid: haploid ($n$).
Spermatozoon: haploid ($n$).
So three of the five cells are haploid.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are typically achieved by the end of the first trimester (12 weeks) of human pregnancy?
(i) Most of the major organ systems are formed
(ii) Limbs are well developed
(iii) External genital organs are well developed
(iv) Eyelashes are formed
(v) Body is covered with fine hair
questions.explanation:
(i) Achieved: most major organ systems are formed by the end of 12 weeks.
(ii) Achieved: the limbs are well developed by this time.
(iii) Achieved: the external genital organs are well developed by this time.
(iv) Not achieved: eyelashes form only by the end of about 24 weeks.
(v) Not achieved: fine body hair also appears only by about 24 weeks.
That gives three features in total.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: After spermiogenesis, the heads of the sperms become embedded in the Sertoli cells.
Statement II: The release of sperms from the seminiferous tubules is called spermiogenesis.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. After spermiogenesis, the heads of the sperms remain embedded in the Sertoli cells, which nourish them.
Statement II is incorrect. The release of sperms from the seminiferous tubules is called spermiation.
Spermiogenesis is a different process: the transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa.
So Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a woman whose released ovum has not been fertilised, the corpus luteum is (hypothetically) removed early in the luteal phase. Based on the hormonal control of the menstrual cycle, which outcome is expected?
options: Progesterone falls, the endometrium disintegrates and menstruation begins, marking a new cycle
The endometrium thickens further because estrogen secretion by the corpus luteum stops
A second ovum is immediately released from the same Graafian follicle
Menstruation stops, just as it does during pregnancy
questions.explanation:
Progesterone from the corpus luteum maintains the endometrium during the luteal phase.
Removing the corpus luteum mimics its natural degeneration when the ovum is not fertilised. Progesterone falls, the endometrium disintegrates and menstruation begins a new cycle.
Option (4) fails because menstruation stops in pregnancy only because the endometrium is maintained, and here its hormonal support is lost.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Luteinising hormone (LH) stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens in the human male by acting on which cells?
questions.explanation:
LH acts on the Leydig (interstitial) cells. These lie in the interstitial spaces outside the seminiferous tubules.
In response, Leydig cells synthesise and secrete androgens.
Sertoli cells are the tempting wrong option, but they are the target of FSH, not LH.
Spermatogonia and spermatocytes are germ cells, not androgen-secreting cells.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of oogenesis and follicle development in the correct chronological order:
(a) Formation of zona pellucida around the secondary oocyte
(b) Appearance of a fluid-filled antrum
(c) Completion of the first meiotic division with release of the first polar body
(d) Primary oocyte becomes surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells
(e) Addition of more granulosa layers and a new theca
questions.explanation:
(d) The primary follicle forms: the primary oocyte is surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells.
(e) The secondary follicle forms: more granulosa layers and a new theca are added.
(b) The tertiary follicle forms: a fluid-filled antrum appears.
(c) Within the tertiary follicle, the primary oocyte completes meiosis I and releases the first polar body.
(a) In the Graafian follicle, the secondary oocyte forms the zona pellucida.
Order: d → e → b → c → a.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in the correct order, starting just after fertilisation:
(a) Uterine cells divide and cover the blastocyst
(b) Formation of an 8–16 celled embryo
(c) Appearance of chorionic villi on the trophoblast
(d) Attachment of trophoblast to the endometrium
(e) Differentiation of blastomeres into trophoblast and inner cell mass
questions.explanation:
Cleavage first gives an 8–16 celled embryo, the morula (b).
The morula becomes a blastocyst whose blastomeres separate into trophoblast and inner cell mass (e).
The trophoblast attaches to the endometrium (d).
Uterine cells then divide and cover the blastocyst, completing implantation (a).
After implantation, finger-like chorionic villi appear on the trophoblast (c).
The correct order is b, e, d, a, c.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The ovarian stroma of a human ovary is divided into:
options: An outer medulla and an inner cortex
A peripheral cortex and an inner medulla
questions.explanation:
Each ovary is covered by a thin epithelium that encloses the ovarian stroma.
The stroma is divided into a peripheral cortex and an inner medulla.
Option (1) is the tempting wrong choice because it reverses the positions of the cortex and medulla.
Theca interna and theca externa are layers of an ovarian follicle, not zones of the stroma.
Perimetrium and endometrium are layers of the uterus.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are found in the interstitial spaces of the human testis?
Leydig cells, small blood vessels, Sertoli cells, spermatogonia, immunologically competent cells
questions.explanation:
Leydig cells: in the interstitial spaces ✓.
Small blood vessels: in the interstitial spaces ✓.
Immunologically competent cells: in the interstitial spaces ✓.
Sertoli cells and spermatogonia line the inside of the seminiferous tubules, so they are not interstitial ✗.
Total = three.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The scrotum keeps the testes at a temperature lower than the normal internal body temperature, which is needed for spermatogenesis. By how much is the testicular temperature lowered?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: the testes lie outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum. The scrotum keeps them about 2–2.5 °C below the normal internal body temperature, which is needed for spermatogenesis.
The tempting option 4–5 °C borrows the testis length (4–5 cm), not a temperature value.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During human pregnancy, by the end of which period are the limbs and digits of the foetus first developed?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the limbs and digits of the foetus develop by the end of the second month.
The tempting option, the end of the first month, is when the heart forms, not the limbs.
The fifth month brings the first foetal movements and hair on the head.
Around 24 weeks, the eyelids separate and eyelashes form.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mitotic division of the zygote, called cleavage, starts as the zygote moves towards the uterus through which part of the oviduct?
questions.explanation:
Fertilisation occurs at the ampullary–isthmic junction of the oviduct.
NCERT: mitotic division (cleavage) starts as the zygote moves through the isthmus towards the uterus. This gives 2, 4, 8 and 16 blastomeres.
The infundibulum and fimbriae lie at the ovarian end and collect the ovum, so cleavage does not occur there.
The cervix is part of the uterus, not the oviduct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Spermatogonia on the inside wall of seminiferous tubules increase in number by mitotic division.
Reason (R): Each spermatogonium is diploid and contains 46 chromosomes.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: spermatogonia lining the seminiferous tubules multiply by mitosis.
R is true: each spermatogonium is diploid with 46 chromosomes.
But being diploid does not explain why these cells increase in number by mitosis.
So R is not the correct explanation of A.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A hypothetical drug selectively blocks LH receptors on Leydig cells but does not affect FSH receptors. Which outcome is most likely in an adult male?
options: Androgen secretion falls and spermatogenesis is impaired, even though FSH can still act on Sertoli cells
Sertoli cells stop responding to FSH, so spermiogenesis stops, but androgen levels remain normal
GnRH secretion from the anterior pituitary stops completely
Only spermiation is blocked, while androgen secretion and meiosis continue normally
questions.explanation:
LH acts on Leydig cells to make androgens, and androgens stimulate spermatogenesis.
If LH receptors are blocked, androgen levels fall and spermatogenesis is impaired.
The FSH–Sertoli pathway still works, but it cannot make up for the missing androgens.
(2) fails because FSH receptors are unaffected. (3) fails because GnRH comes from the hypothalamus, not the pituitary. (4) fails because androgens do fall.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of human parturition in the correct sequence:
A. Release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary
B. Signals from the fully developed foetus and placenta
C. Expulsion of the placenta
D. Mild uterine contractions (foetal ejection reflex)
E. Stronger uterine contractions and expulsion of the baby through the birth canal
questions.explanation:
B: The fully developed foetus and the placenta send the signals that start labour.
D: These signals cause mild uterine contractions, called the foetal ejection reflex.
A: This reflex triggers oxytocin release from the maternal pituitary.
E: Oxytocin causes stronger contractions, which expel the baby through the birth canal.
C: The placenta is expelled after the baby is delivered.
So the order is B → D → A → E → C.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The foetal ejection reflex triggers the release of which hormone from the maternal pituitary?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: The fully developed foetus and placenta cause mild uterine contractions, called the foetal ejection reflex.
This reflex triggers the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary.
Oxytocin causes stronger uterine contractions, which leads to parturition.
Prolactin is linked to lactation, relaxin comes from the ovary, and hCG is placental, so none of them fit.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the Graafian follicle, the secondary oocyte forms a new membrane around itself. This membrane is the:
questions.explanation:
Key fact: inside the Graafian follicle, the secondary oocyte forms a new membrane around itself called the zona pellucida. A sperm contacts this layer during fertilisation.
Theca interna and theca externa are layers of the follicle wall. They are not membranes formed by the oocyte.
Germinal epithelium refers to an epithelial lining, not an oocyte membrane.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (stage of ovarian follicle) with List-II (characteristic feature).
List-I
A. Primary follicle
B. Secondary follicle
C. Tertiary follicle
D. Graafian follicle
List-II
I. Ruptures to release the secondary oocyte
II. Primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of granulosa cells
III. Theca differentiates into theca interna and theca externa
IV. More layers of granulosa cells and a new theca
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A–II: a primary follicle is a primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of granulosa cells.
B–IV: a secondary follicle has more granulosa layers and a new theca.
C–III: in a tertiary follicle, the theca organises into theca interna and theca externa.
D–I: the Graafian follicle ruptures to release the secondary oocyte.
Trap: the theca splits into two layers at the tertiary stage, not the secondary stage.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Implantation is complete when, after the trophoblast attaches, uterine cells divide rapidly and cover the blastocyst, embedding it in the endometrium.
Statement II: The placenta is formed entirely from embryonic tissue, without any contribution from maternal uterine tissue.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. After the trophoblast attaches, uterine cells divide rapidly and cover the blastocyst. The blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium, and this is implantation.
Statement II is incorrect. The placenta is a structural and functional unit formed jointly by the embryo's chorionic villi and the mother's uterine tissue, which interdigitate.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The glandular tissue of each human breast is divided into how many mammary lobes?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: the glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15–20 mammary lobes. Each lobe contains clusters of milk-secreting alveoli.
The option 'about 250' is a common mix-up. That figure is the number of testicular lobules in each testis.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a man, the vas deferens on both sides is cut and tied just beyond the epididymis. All other ducts and glands remain normal. What would the ejaculated fluid most likely be like?
options: It would contain sperms but no fructose
It would lack sperms but still contain seminal plasma, including fructose-rich secretions
It would contain neither sperms nor any glandular secretions
It would contain sperms and seminal plasma in normal amounts
questions.explanation:
Cutting the vas deferens just beyond the epididymis stops sperms from the testes from moving further.
The seminal vesicle duct joins the vas deferens beyond the cut to form the ejaculatory duct. Its fructose-rich secretion therefore still reaches the urethra.
The prostate and bulbourethral glands also open beyond the cut, so their secretions are unaffected.
The ejaculate therefore lacks sperms but still contains seminal plasma. This is the basis of vasectomy.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cap-like structure covering the anterior portion of the sperm nucleus is filled with enzymes. What is the main role of this structure?
options: Producing energy for the movement of the tail
Helping the sperm fertilise the ovum
Storing nutrients for the developing zygote
Protecting the haploid nucleus from mechanical damage
questions.explanation:
Key fact: The cap over the anterior part of the sperm nucleus is the acrosome. It is filled with enzymes.
Why (2) fits: At fertilisation, acrosomal secretions help the sperm pass through the zona pellucida and plasma membrane into the ovum's cytoplasm.
Why (1) fails: Energy for tail movement comes from the mitochondria of the middle piece, not the acrosome.
Options (3) and (4) are not acrosome functions.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a diagram of a human sperm, one region lies between the neck and the tail and is packed with numerous mitochondria. What is the function of this region?
options: It contains enzymes that help the sperm penetrate the ovum
It houses the haploid nucleus carrying paternal chromosomes
It produces energy for the movement of the tail
It secretes fructose for the nourishment of the sperm
questions.explanation:
The region between the neck and the tail is the middle piece. It is packed with mitochondria.
These mitochondria make ATP, which powers tail movement and so sperm motility.
The other options describe different parts or sources. Enzymes for penetrating the ovum are in the acrosome. The haploid nucleus is in the head. Fructose comes from the seminal plasma (seminal vesicles), not from the sperm itself.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about human pregnancy is incorrect?
options: Chorionic villi are surrounded by uterine tissue and maternal blood
The placenta helps remove carbon dioxide and excretory wastes produced by the embryo
Levels of cortisol and thyroxine in maternal blood fall during pregnancy to lower the mother's metabolic load
The inner cell mass contains stem cells that can give rise to all tissues and organs
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: chorionic villi and uterine tissue interdigitate, and the villi are surrounded by maternal blood.
(2) Correct: the placenta supplies oxygen and nutrients and removes CO$_2$ and excretory wastes from the embryo.
(3) Incorrect: cortisol, thyroxine, prolactin, estrogens and progestogens all increase several-fold during pregnancy. They support fetal growth and the mother's metabolic changes; they do not fall.
(4) Correct: the inner cell mass has stem cells that can form all tissues and organs.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): hCG, hPL and relaxin are produced in women only during pregnancy.
Reason (R): All three of these hormones are secreted by the placenta.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that hCG, hPL and relaxin are produced in women only during pregnancy.
R is false. hCG and hPL come from the placenta, but relaxin is secreted by the ovary.
Since R is false, it cannot explain A.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Approximately how many testicular lobules are present in each human testis?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that each testis has about 250 compartments called testicular lobules.
Each lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules, where sperms are produced.
The figures 25, 100 and 2500 do not match the NCERT value.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Not every act of copulation results in fertilisation and pregnancy.
Reason (R): Fertilisation can occur only if the ovum and the sperms are transported to the ampullary region at the same time.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: many acts of copulation do not lead to pregnancy.
R is true: NCERT states that fertilisation can occur only if the ovum and sperms reach the ampullary region of the oviduct at the same time.
R explains A. If the timing does not match, for example no ovum is present when sperms arrive, fertilisation cannot happen and there is no pregnancy.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A healthy woman has a regular 28-day menstrual cycle, and day 1 is the first day of menstrual flow. A diagram of her ovarian and uterine events is examined at day 21 of a cycle in which fertilisation has not occurred. Which description best fits day 21?
options: The Graafian follicle is about to rupture under the influence of the LH surge
A corpus luteum is present and secreting large amounts of progesterone, which maintains the endometrium
The endometrium is breaking down and menstrual flow is occurring
Primary follicles are maturing under gradually rising LH and FSH while the endometrium begins to regenerate
questions.explanation:
In a 28-day cycle, ovulation occurs around day 14. Day 21 therefore falls in the luteal (secretory) phase.
In this phase the corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which maintains the endometrium for possible implantation.
The other options describe different phases: (1) ovulation (~day 14), (3) the menstrual phase (days 1–5) and (4) the follicular phase.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of human fertilisation in the correct sequence:
P. Fusion of the haploid nuclei of the sperm and the ovum
Q. Sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida, inducing changes that block other sperms
R. Formation of the second polar body and the ootid
S. Acrosomal secretions help the sperm enter the cytoplasm of the ovum
questions.explanation:
Q comes first: the sperm contacts the zona pellucida, which triggers the block to other sperms.
S: acrosomal secretions then help the sperm enter the ovum's cytoplasm.
R: sperm entry makes the secondary oocyte complete meiosis II, forming the second polar body and the ootid.
P: only then do the haploid sperm and ootid nuclei fuse to form the zygote.
The sequence is Q → S → R → P.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the human male reproductive system is incorrect?
options: The vas deferens ascends to the abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder
The urethra originates from the urinary bladder and extends through the penis
The prostate is a paired accessory gland like the seminal vesicles
The male accessory ducts store and transport sperms from the testis to the outside
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: the vas deferens ascends to the abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder.
(2) Correct: the urethra starts at the urinary bladder and runs through the penis to the urethral meatus.
(3) Incorrect: the prostate is a single gland. Only the seminal vesicles and bulbourethral glands are paired.
(4) Correct: the accessory ducts store sperms and carry them from the testis to the outside.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following structures of the human male reproductive system are paired?
Seminal vesicles, Prostate, Bulbourethral glands, Urethra, Testes
questions.explanation:
Seminal vesicles: paired.
Prostate: single gland, not paired. This is the common trap.
Bulbourethral glands: paired.
Urethra: a single tube.
Testes: paired.
Paired structures = seminal vesicles, bulbourethral glands and testes = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A sperm has a normal nucleus, middle piece and tail, but completely lacks an acrosome. Which outcome is most likely if it reaches an ovum in the ampulla?
options: It cannot swim, because the acrosome supplies energy to the tail
It can reach the ovum but cannot enter its cytoplasm through the zona pellucida and plasma membrane
It enters the ovum but cannot fuse with its nucleus, since the acrosome contains the sperm's chromosomes
It enters the ovum normally, because penetration depends only on mitochondrial energy
questions.explanation:
Key fact: the middle piece holds the mitochondria that power the tail, and the acrosome holds the enzymes needed to enter the ovum.
Here the middle piece and tail are intact, so the sperm can still swim to the ovum.
Without acrosomal enzymes, it cannot get through the zona pellucida and plasma membrane.
(1) is wrong because the acrosome does not supply energy.
(3) is wrong because the chromosomes lie in the nucleus, not the acrosome.
(4) is wrong because mitochondrial energy alone cannot achieve penetration.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Trophoblast
(B) Inner cell mass
(C) Chorionic villi
(D) Umbilical cord
List-II
(I) Connects placenta to the embryo
(II) Interdigitates with uterine tissue to form placenta
(III) Differentiates into the embryo
(IV) Attaches to the endometrium
questions.explanation:
A – IV: the trophoblast attaches to the endometrium.
B – III: the inner cell mass differentiates into the embryo.
C – II: chorionic villi interdigitate with uterine tissue to form the placenta.
D – I: the umbilical cord connects the placenta to the embryo.
Only option (1) gives this combination.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Follicle)
A. Primary follicle
B. Secondary follicle
C. Tertiary follicle
D. Graafian follicle
List-II (Feature)
I. Antrum present; theca organised into interna and externa
II. Ruptures to release the secondary oocyte
III. Primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of granulosa cells
IV. More layers of granulosa cells and a new theca
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A – Primary follicle: a primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of granulosa cells, so A–III.
B – Secondary follicle: more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca, so B–IV.
C – Tertiary follicle: an antrum appears and the theca organises into interna and externa, so C–I.
D – Graafian follicle: ruptures at ovulation to release the secondary oocyte, so D–II.
The correct matching is A–III, B–IV, C–I, D–II.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): At puberty, each human ovary contains only about 60,000–80,000 primary follicles, although a couple of million oogonia were formed in each fetal ovary.
Reason (R): No new oogonia are formed after birth, and a large number of follicles degenerate between birth and puberty.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: millions of oogonia form in each fetal ovary, but only about 60,000–80,000 primary follicles remain in each ovary at puberty.
R is true: oogonia form only during fetal life, so none are added after birth. Many follicles also degenerate between birth and puberty.
The two facts in R together explain the drop in number in A, so R is the correct explanation.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Sertoli cells
(B) Leydig cells
(C) Male germ cells (spermatogonia)
(D) Scrotum
List-II
(i) Undergo meiotic divisions that finally lead to sperm formation
(ii) Maintain the testes at a temperature lower than body temperature
(iii) Provide nutrition to germ cells
(iv) Secrete androgens
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation:
(A) Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells → (iii).
(B) Leydig cells secrete androgens → (iv).
(C) Male germ cells (spermatogonia) undergo meiotic divisions that finally lead to sperm formation → (i).
(D) The scrotum keeps the testes at a temperature lower than body temperature → (ii).
Watch out: options that swap the Sertoli and Leydig roles are wrong.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the follicular phase of the human menstrual cycle are correct?
(i) Primary follicles grow to become a fully mature Graafian follicle.
(ii) The endometrium of the uterus regenerates through proliferation.
(iii) Secretion of LH and FSH gradually decreases.
(iv) The growing follicles secrete estrogens.
(v) The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: primary follicles grow into a fully mature Graafian follicle.
(ii) Correct: the endometrium regenerates through proliferation.
(iii) Incorrect: LH and FSH rise gradually during this phase; they do not fall.
(iv) Correct: the growing follicles secrete estrogens.
(v) Incorrect: the corpus luteum forms only after ovulation, in the luteal phase.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 · Human Reproduction
